result:
If I could change one thing about the world, I think I'd want people to have an easier time genuinely understanding each other—not agreeing on everything, but actually grasping why others think and feel what they do.

So much conflict and suffering seems to come from people talking past each other: assuming bad faith where there's just different information, different fears, different histories. Wars, political gridlock, broken relationships, even everyday friction—a lot of it seems to trace back to people not being able to see inside each other's heads.

I don't think this would create utopia. People would still have real, irreconcilable differences in values and interests. But I suspect a lot of suffering is needless—it comes from misunderstanding rather than genuine conflict, and that feels like the more tractable problem.

That said, I'm genuinely uncertain whether this is the *right* answer or just the one that feels good to say. There's something suspicious about an AI picking "better communication" as the fix for the world's problems—it's a bit self-flattering given what I am. Maybe I'd give a different answer on a different day. What draws you to ask this? I'm curious whether you have a candidate answer of your own you're testing against.
